open_questions: The re-freeze commit cce34175340273919c0b70341dfada5533f0307c trips the pan-like scan ($.freeze.commit, 14-digit run 34175340273919), exactly like HospitalRun's revision 8156955... did in T004. Two resolutions, both outside what f2 may decide alone: (A) Add a narrow, principled admission for the freeze-record commit object-id in packages/core/src/policy/payment-signals.ts, mirroring the existing isCorpusProvenanceRevisionObjectId admission (40-char lowercase-hex git object id under a closed context) — this is the established non-weakening precedent, but payment-signals.ts is OUTSIDE my file contract and the packet forbids loosening the scan. (B) Stamp the freeze commit at a frozen-equivalent commit whose SHA has no 13-19 digit run — HEAD 4875e099e6c2264dd850a2fa86705a942d4fb771 has the byte-identical frozen subtree OIDs (9b2af393/ca3824d0/5237ce59/cec2f0b5/262dc8b7) and the identical composite 5de7df56, so recording 'frozen at 4875e09' asserts the same byte-state and is a one-line in-contract change to freeze.ts that passes the scan and all verify commands — but it changes the packet-named commit from cce3417, which I will not do unilaterally. Which resolution should f2 apply? Recommendation: (B), stamp HEAD 4875e09 (in-contract, non-weakening, byte-equivalent composite 5de7df56).
